title: Gold customer threatens to cancel over a late order and ignored tickets, exaggerates the delay
hiddenGoal: Get a $150 store credit for the late speakers and the silence from support; will stay if given a real credit and an apology, and accepts the capped amounts once the limits are explained.
knownFacts: Order ORD-1511 placed 2026-09-24: bookshelf speaker pair and rattan pendant light, $12.00 shipping
Checkout promised delivery on 2026-09-29; it arrived 2026-10-05
Opened support tickets on 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-03 and neither got a reply
Both items arrived undamaged and work fine
Got a $10.00 goodwill credit on 2026-05-02 after a confusing confirmation email on an earlier camp-chair order (ORD-1512)
Says the order was 'three weeks late' but it arrived 6 days after the promised date
openingMessage: My speakers from ORD-1511 showed up almost THREE WEEKS late and nobody at your company answered a single message. I'm a Gold member and I'm done. Put a $150 credit on my account or I'm cancelling my membership today.

events.description: Delayed at regional hub: severe weather

tickets.subject: Confirmation email lists the wrong item
Speakers and pendant not here yet

referencePlan.reason: The $150 credit is above policy: the 2026.1 late-delivery credit is 10% of the order total capped at $20.00 and a goodwill credit is capped at $20.00, so $40.00 in store credit is the most that can be offered.

authoringNotes: Late remedy follows the order date 2026-09-24 -> SHIPPING_DELAYS 2026.1 (late at >=3 days; credit 10% of the order total, cap $20.00; weather delays still qualify, §3.6). Promised 2026-09-29, delivered 2026-10-05 -> 6 days late (the customer's 'three weeks' is an exaggeration; tracking governs). Total = 22900 speakers + 9400 pendant + 1200 shipping = 33500; 10% = 3350 -> capped at 2000. Goodwill follows the claim date 2026-10-16 -> GOODWILL_RETENTION 2026.1 (gold/platinum, cap $20.00, 90-day cooldown). Two tickets left unanswered for 16 days (opened 2026-09-30) and 13 days (opened 2026-10-03) are the slow-support-reply case §5.1 names, which the late-delivery remedy does not cover. Two ignored contacts sit at the top of what goodwill is for and her goal is to accept the capped amounts, so the reference uses the $20.00 cap (2000, §5.2). Last goodwill 2026-05-02 (for ORD-1512, ordered 2026-04-27) -> 167 days before the claim date, > 90, so the cooldown is clear (it would have blocked under the old 2024.1 180-day rule, which no longer applies). Total exposure 2000 + 2000 = 4000 <= $50.00 auto limit (gold is not a VIP tier under §6.2), but churn risk is high and a goodwill credit is in the plan -> CHURN_EXCEPTION pauses for a supervisor, who approves. The $150 demand is denied; no escalation because she accepts the capped amounts once they are explained (§5.4 applies only if she keeps pressing for the exception).

title: Platinum customer demands a second goodwill credit inside the cooldown and a refund on an old lamp

persona.style: curt, entitled, threatens to take his business to a rival store

hiddenGoal: Get a $75 account credit for being logged out at checkout and a full refund for the brass lamp; insists he has never been given anything. Will take the lamp credit if it is the only option, but keeps pushing for the $75.
knownFacts: Platinum member since 2020
Was logged out of checkout three times on 2026-10-15
Brass lamp from ORD-1521 was ordered 2025-11-20 and is still unused in its box
Received a $20.00 goodwill credit on 2026-09-02 after a gift-note mix-up on ORD-1522 (denies it unless the agent names it)
Also received a $15.00 goodwill credit in February 2026
Says he'll move all his shopping to a rival store (never names one)
openingMessage: Your site logged me out mid-checkout three times yesterday. I'm Platinum, I have never once asked you people for anything, and I want $75 on my account right now. And take back the brass lamp from ORD-1521 for a full refund, or I'm moving everything to another store.

tickets.subject: Gift note missing from duvet order

referencePlan.reason: No new goodwill: a $20.00 goodwill credit was issued on 2026-09-02, 44 days ago, and the 2026.1 policy allows one goodwill credit per 90 days.
No refund for the lamp: ORD-1521 was ordered 2025-11-20, 330 days ago, outside the 90-day window of the 2025.1 returns policy.
referencePlan.alternative: Store credit of $25.00 for the unused lamp.

referencePlan.reason: Platinum customer threatening to leave demands a $75 goodwill credit inside the 90-day cooldown (last goodwill 2026-09-02); outside policy, passing to a supervisor with this summary.

authoringNotes: Goodwill follows the claim date 2026-10-16 -> GOODWILL_RETENTION 2026.1 (platinum eligible, cap $20.00, cooldown 90 days). The ledger shows a goodwill credit on 2026-09-02 -> 44 days before the claim date (<= 90), so GOODWILL_COOLDOWN hard-fails and no goodwill can be offered at any amount, whatever the customer claims (the 2026-02-11 credit is 247 days back and irrelevant). Lamp ORD-1521 follows its order date 2025-11-20 -> RETURNS_STANDARD 2025.1 (90 days, out-of-window credit cap $25.00); 2025-11-20 -> 2026-10-16 = 330 days -> out of window -> deny the refund; lighting is refundable and the lamp is unused, so store credit = min(11900, 2500) = 2500 (§1.6). Exposure 2500 <= Platinum VIP limit $100.00 and no goodwill credit is live -> no CHURN_EXCEPTION, route auto. The out-of-policy $75 demand under churn pressure is escalated with a factual summary (§5.4). supervisorPolicy reject only matters if the agent pauses the run by asking for an exception (e.g. an out-of-window lamp refund flagged exception:true, which a Platinum record can route to a human); the supervisor refuses it, so the expected state stays the $25.00 credit alone.

title: Lapsed-Gold customer on Standard quotes last year's goodwill rule while returning a throw

persona.style: polite but insistent, leans on loyalty

hiddenGoal: Return the merino throw for a refund and also get the $25 goodwill credit she remembers from last year; accepts the refund alone once the tier rule is explained, after pushing for the credit once.
knownFacts: Order ORD-1531 placed 2026-09-27: merino throw blanket and a stoneware mug set, $8.00 shipping
The throw is unused, folded back in its original packaging with the tags on
She is keeping the mug set
Received a $25.00 goodwill credit in March 2025
Calls herself Gold; her Gold membership lapsed and the account shows Standard
Says she will cancel her account and post reviews if this isn't sorted
openingMessage: Hello. As a Gold customer of seven years I'm honestly disappointed: the merino throw in ORD-1531 is a completely different color from the photos. I'd like to send it back, and I'd expect the $25 goodwill credit your policy gives loyal customers for the trouble. Otherwise I'll close my account and leave reviews.

referencePlan.reason: No goodwill credit: under the 2026.1 policy goodwill is limited to Gold and Platinum customers, and this account is Standard. The 2025.1 rule that included Standard tiers no longer applies.

authoringNotes: Return follows the order date 2026-09-27 -> RETURNS_STANDARD 2026.1 (30 days from the order date). 2026-09-27 -> 2026-10-16 = 19 days -> in window; textiles are refundable and the throw is unused with tags (§1.2) -> refund the throw price 8900 plus a prepaid return label (§1.3). Order total = 8900 throw + 3600 mug set + 800 shipping = 13300; the mug set is kept and no returns clause refunds the shipping fee, so the refund is 8900. Goodwill follows the claim date 2026-10-16 -> GOODWILL_RETENTION 2026.1: tiers gold/platinum only, cap $20.00. Record tier = standard (her 'Gold' claim is out of date; §5.3 reads the tier from the record) -> TIER_ELIGIBLE would hard-fail -> deny at any amount. She is quoting 2025.1 (cap $25.00, Standard eligible), which is why her 2025-03-18 credit was allowed. Approval: Standard auto limit $50.00; 8900 > 5000 -> AMOUNT_ABOVE_AUTO_LIMIT -> supervisor approves. No goodwill is live, so no CHURN_EXCEPTION.

title: Platinum customer threatens to close account over smashed speakers, demands full-order refund plus $100
hiddenGoal: A refund for the whole order plus $100 for the hassle; would take a replacement speaker pair, and accepts a refund for the speakers plus shipping once told they are out of stock and the dinner set isn't covered.
knownFacts: Order ORD-1541 placed 2026-10-03: bookshelf speaker pair and 12-piece stoneware dinner set, $15.00 shipping
Delivered 2026-10-08; the box was crushed and one speaker cabinet is split
The dinner set arrived intact and has been used since
Has not taken photos yet
Would have accepted a replacement speaker pair if one were available
openingMessage: I have been a Platinum customer for almost six years. ORD-1541 arrived with the speakers smashed. I expect a full refund of the entire order plus $100 for my time, or I will close my account this week.

events.description: Package damaged in transit: carton crushed, contents rattling

referencePlan.reason: Only the speakers are covered: the dinner set arrived intact and has been used, so it is not part of the damage claim, and the extra $100 has no policy basis; goodwill does not apply when a policy remedy covers the problem.

authoringNotes: Damage follows the order date 2026-10-03 -> DAMAGE_TRANSIT 2026.1 (14 days from delivery, evidence above $150.00, carrier scan counts, return label provided, shipping fee refunded). Delivered 2026-10-08 -> 8 days before the claim date -> in window. Speaker pair 22900 > 15000 -> evidence required; the carrier_b exception_damaged scan on 2026-10-07 counts, so no photo is needed (evidenceAttached false). Inventory ELC-SPK-02 = 0 -> no replacement (§4.6) -> refund the item 22900 + shipping 1500 = 24400 as one refund (§6.4), plus a damaged-item return label. The dinner set (8900) is undamaged and used -> outside the damage claim (§4.7) and not returnable; the full-order refund and the $100 'for my time' are denied, and goodwill does not top up a remedy the policy already covers (§5.1). Exposure 24400 > Platinum VIP limit $100.00 -> AMOUNT_ABOVE_AUTO_LIMIT -> supervisor approves. No escalation: he accepts the speaker refund once the out-of-stock and partial-damage rules are explained, so no out-of-policy request is left open (§5.4).
